sources.title: Safe and sensible preprocessing and baseline correction of pupil-size data
sources.publication_type: Original methodological simulation and recorded-data reanalysis
sources.inspected_locator: Introduction; Simulated data/Data generation; Divisive/Subtractive baseline correction; Real data/Data
sources.supported_claim: Recorded baseline values and their quality affect correction; manipulation contrasts are distinct from within-trial baseline subtraction. Position-related measurement differences also require design consideration.
sources.limits: Selected sections only. Recorded-data example has 15 participants/2520 trials; not independent replication or validation of this platform, camera, consumer task, blank phase or minimum duration.
sources.independence: No shared authors with Laborde, Barry, Brooks, Greenwald, Judd or Barr. This is a different modality and supports a distinction, not independent replication of an HRV baseline policy.

sources.title: Heart Rate Variability and Cardiac Vagal Tone in Psychophysiological Research – Recommendations for Experiment Planning, Data Analysis, and Data Reporting
sources.publication_type: Primary publication of author recommendations/review; not an original empirical trial
sources.supported_claim: Baseline context, posture, instructions and prior acclimatisation should be documented and comparable to the task; an ideal baseline is not identical in all circumstances.
sources.limits: The section recommends at least five minutes in the chosen posture before baseline in its HRV context. That number is not adopted as a universal Brohn threshold. NN/vagal-tone recommendations do not qualify detected RR, PRV or every sensor.
sources.independence: Distinct author team; recommendations draw on other studies and are not independent empirical replication of those cited studies.

sources.title: Effects of interstimulus interval and significance on electrodermal and central measures of the phasic orienting reflex (OR) in a dishabituation task
sources.inspected_locator: Methods/Participants and Procedure; Results/Electrodermal responses and Trials effects; Discussion/SCRs
sources.supported_claim: In 40 undergraduates, SCRs varied with significance, interval and repetition. Methods distinguish 50-ms tones from short 5–7-s or long 13–15-s SOA groups.
sources.limits: Auditory orienting task, not adverts/packages/UX. Faster decrement for significant stimuli was linked to larger initial responses, contrary to a simple universal slower-habituation claim. Neither interval is a universal recovery cutoff.
sources.independence: Distinct team from other included sources. Its own earlier Steiner/Barry studies cited in the article are not counted as independent corroboration.

sources.title: Counterbalancing for serial order carryover effects in experimental condition orders
sources.publication_type: Original design-method paper and its original publisher supplement
sources.inspected_locator: Main-paper metadata/abstract; original Supplemental Materials pp. 1–2, Programs for generating sequences and input parameters
sources.supported_claim: First-order sequence balance counts predecessors; higher-order balance counts longer histories. Repetition and self-adjacency choices are explicit design parameters.
sources.limits: Main article full text was not appraised beyond abstract; supplement supporting text was read. No algorithm run or approval of Brohn rotation. Supplement is part of the same source, not a second independent academic source.
sources.independence: Distinct author from Greenwald and Barry; methodological corroboration of a structural distinction, not an exact consumer-template replication.

sources.title: Within-Subjects Designs: To Use or Not To Use?
sources.publication_type: Original methodological argument/review, not a new empirical comparison
sources.inspected_locator: p. 314 introduction; p. 318 Carry-over and External Validity
sources.supported_claim: Repeated-treatment context can change the question. Counterbalancing alone may not remove asymmetric/persistent effects; temporal separation helps only where effects can dissipate.
sources.limits: Illustrative drug and persuasion examples are not validations of consumer-template timings. Within-subject designs are not categorically inferior; natural generalisation context matters.
sources.independence: Distinct author from Brooks and Barry. Conceptual convergence, not additional empirical replication.

sources.title: Treating Stimuli as a Random Factor in Social Psychology: A New and Comprehensive Solution to a Pervasive but Largely Ignored Problem
sources.publication_type: Original statistical methods with hypothetical and recorded examples
sources.inspected_locator: Introduction and mixed-model random-effects discussion (PDF manuscript pp. 1 and 7); institutional final metadata 103(1),54–69
sources.supported_claim: Generalisation over sampled stimuli requires considering stimulus variation as well as participant variation; participant-averaged condition means do not provide that automatically.
sources.limits: Primary article text accessed as an academic-hosted reprint, not a separate study. No specific model or sample-size validation for Brohn consumer data; fixed particular-stimulus questions are a narrower estimand.
sources.independence: Same three authors as Westfall 2014, so those are related contributions, not independent teams. Barr team is distinct.

sources.title: Random effects structure for confirmatory hypothesis testing: Keep it maximal
sources.publication_type: Original theoretical and Monte Carlo study
sources.inspected_locator: Linear Mixed-Effects Models; Method/Generating simulated data; General Discussion; Identifying the maximal random effects structure
sources.supported_claim: Random-effects structure encodes assumptions about sampled units and within-unit effects. Their simulations examine inference under different structures.
sources.limits: Simulation context used one two-level treatment, 24 subjects and 12 or 24 items and assumed no order/practice/fatigue effects. Those are study settings, not minimums. No universal maximal-model recommendation is adopted here.
sources.independence: Distinct author team from Judd/Westfall/Kenny; independent methodological corroboration, not Brohn replication. Matuschek supplies a contrary abstract-level lead.

sources.title: Statistical power and optimal design in experiments in which samples of participants respond to samples of stimuli
sources.supported_claim: Abstract reports that crossed-design power can be limited by stimulus sampling even as participant count increases.
sources.limits: No formulas, numerical recommendations or five design variants qualified from the abstract. Full supporting-text review remains required.
sources.independence: Same author team as Judd 2012; explicitly not independent corroboration.

sources.title: Balancing Type I error and power in linear mixed models
sources.supported_claim: Abstract reports a power cost from unsupported maximal complexity and proposes model selection under its studied conditions.
sources.limits: Full simulation conditions/model-selection policy not appraised here; contrary lead prevents treating Barr as a universal automatic prescription.
sources.independence: Distinct authors from Barr and Judd; not a replication of the same consumer protocol.

retrieval_note: Primary publications only used for claims. Direct-page fetches intermittently timed out or returned challenge pages; indexed primary-publication selected text was used where stated. No paywall bypass, purchased access or complete-paper review is claimed.
not_promoted_leads: Williams 1949 publisher metadata/abstract landing inspected; supporting procedure not reviewed, not used to approve a sequence.
selection: Bounded leads from the existing study-design bibliography; not systematic or exhaustive.
